data.title: Exit from germinal center to become quiescent memory B cells depends on metabolic reprograming and provision of a survival signal
data.authors: Inoue T; Shinnakasu R; Kawai C; Ise W; Kawakami E; Sax N; Oki T; Kitamura T; Yamashita K; Fukuyama H; Kurosaki T

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Mouse; NP-CGG/alum immunization, adoptive transfer of B1-8 transgenic B cells, inducible knockouts (Bach2/Blimp1, Bcl6, Bim, BCR) and rapamycin in rapamycin-resistant hosts
data.finding: In immunized mice, a small population of germinal-center B cells with lower mTORC1 activity (CD38int Bcl6hi/int Efnb1+, called pro-memory cells) was the one that went on to become memory B cells. Constitutively high mTORC1 activity (Bach2/Blimp1 double-deficient B cells) impaired formation of this population, and rapamycin given to B cells that could respond to it shifted the balance toward memory-prone cells and raised memory B cell numbers (about threefold in the double-deficient cells). Memory B cells made under rapamycin gave similar recall antibody responses. Low mTORC1 was necessary but not sufficient: survival also depended on higher Bcl2 and surface BCR. Boundary: one immunization model (NP-CGG/alum) in mouse spleen, using transferred transgenic B cells; no human data. Rapamycin was tested at one dose and schedule, and the study does not show that lowering mTORC1 improves vaccine responses.
data.abstract_excerpt: A still unanswered question is what drives the small fraction of activated germinal center (GC) B cells to become long-lived quiescent memory B cells. We found here that a small population of GC-derived CD38intBcl6hi/intEfnb1+ cells with lower mTORC1 activity favored the memory B cell fate. Constitutively high mTORC1 activity led to defects in formation of the CD38intBcl6hi/intEfnb1+ cells; conversely, decreasing mTORC1 activity resulted in relative enrichment of this memory-prone population over the recycling-prone one.

extracted_findings.intervention: Rapamycin (0.16 mg/kg i.p. daily, days 4-11 or 4-13 after immunization); inducible deletion of Bach2/Blimp1, Bcl6 (haploinsufficiency), Bim (haploinsufficiency) and BCR in B cells
extracted_findings.target: mTORC1 activity in germinal-center B cells (memory vs recycling fate)
extracted_findings.effect: Lower mTORC1 activity favors the memory B cell fate; high mTORC1 impairs it; rapamycin enriches memory-prone cells and increases memory B cell numbers
extracted_findings.dose: Rapamycin 0.16 mg/kg i.p. once daily, days 4-11 (Bach2/Blimp1 knockout experiment) or days 4-13 (competitive cotransfer experiment) after NP-CGG/alum immunization
extracted_findings.sample_size: Typically n = 3-9 mice per group, 2-4 independent experiments
extracted_findings.effect_size: Rapamycin in Bach2/Blimp1 double-deficient B cells: about threefold more IgG1+ memory B cells (P < 0.05 to < 0.01, unpaired t test)
extracted_findings.limitations: Single immunization model; small n; pS6 and c-Myc did not differ between Fr.3 and Fr.5 cells, so low mTORC1 is necessary but not sufficient; rapamycin only partly rescued memory cell numbers in knockout cells (c-Myc also involved); Bcl6 downregulation in pro-memory cells is small
